record.original_question: For cubic bipartite graphs equipped with a 3-list-assignment, two disjoint proper colorings are known to exist. Does every cubic bipartite graph with a 3-list-assignment also admit three pairwise-disjoint proper list-colorings?

evidence.quote: In the case of cubic bipartite graphs, it is possible to find two disjoint proper colourings (problem similar to Problem 3) [unpublished]. Hence, the following question arises: Is it possible to find three disjoint proper colourings in the case of cubic bipartite graphs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a cubic bipartite graph (every vertex has degree exactly 3, and V admits a bipartition into two independent sets). A k-list-assignment for G is a function L that assigns to every vertex v ∈ V a set L(v) of k colors. A proper L-coloring of G is a function c : V → ⋃_v L(v) such that c(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V and c(u) ≠ c(v) whenever uv ∈ E. A collection c_1, c_2, …, c_t of proper L-colorings is said to be pairwise disjoint if for every vertex v ∈ V the values c_1(v), c_2(v), …, c_t(v) are all distinct.

Question: Is it true that for every cubic bipartite graph G and every 3-list-assignment L of G there exist three pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings of G?
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks whether the list packing number of every cubic bipartite graph is at most 3. The best known general bound is that the list packing number of subcubic graphs is at most 4 (Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, Kang). For complete bipartite graphs the list packing number can exceed the degree, and recent work by Cambie and Kang on packing colorings in complete bipartite graphs and on the correspondence/list packing of bounded-degree graphs has not settled the bipartite cubic case. No published proof that 3 disjoint proper L-colorings always exist for cubic bipartite graphs with 3-list-assignments has been located; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: List packing number of bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Both the list and correspondence packing numbers of subcubic graphs are at most 4.
status_evidence.claim: The general upper bound for subcubic graphs is 4, leaving the question of bound 3 for cubic bipartite graphs unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Packing list-colorings
status_evidence.snippet: An L-packing of G with respect to an L-coloring assignment is a collection of mutually disjoint proper L-colorings.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the framework of list packing relevant to the question.

status_evidence.title: Packing colourings in complete bipartite graphs and the inverse problem for correspondence packing
status_evidence.snippet: Cambie and Kang study packing numbers of bipartite graphs and disprove a related conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on bipartite list packing does not resolve the cubic bipartite case at level 3.
